'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Mali War]]
**Six [[Malian Armed Forces|Malian troops]] are killed and 18 others are injured in simultaneous [[jihadist]] attacks in the central [[Mopti Region]]. The military also stated that around 30 [[militant]]s were also killed in the clashes. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/1/24/six-malian-soldiers-killed-in-complex-and-simultaneous-attacks (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Palmas FR plane crash]]
**A [[plane crash]]es in [[Palmas, Tocantins]], [[Brazil]], killing four [[Palmas Futebol e Regatas]] [[association football|footballers]], their team's president, and the pilot. [https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/esporte/2021/01/24/acidente-mata-presidente-e-quatro-jogadores-do-time-do-palmas (CNN Brasil)]
*Eleven of the [[mining|miners]] who went missing two weeks ago in [[Qixia, Shandong|Qixia]], [[Shandong]], [[China]], after the [[gold mine]] where they worked [[mining accident|collapsed]], are rescued alive. Another miner is found dead, while ten others are still missing. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-55784231 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****[[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
*****The [[Israel]]i [[Cabinet of Israel|cabinet]] agrees to close [[Ben Gurion International Airport]] and ban all incoming and outgoing international passengers from the airport, beginning at midnight tomorrow. [[Cargo aircraft|Cargo flights]], medical evacuations and [[firefighting]] flights are exempted from this rule. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/middle_east/israel-coronavirus-ben-gurion-airport-closed/2021/01/24/be24f790-5e67-11eb-9430-e7c77b5b0297_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
****[[Social impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
*****Clashes broke out in three cities across [[Israel]] as police attempted to enforce coronavirus lockdown restrictions in a number of [[ultra-Orthodox]] communities. [[Israel]] is currently in a [[COVID-19 pandemic]] [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdown|lockdown]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/ultra-orthodox-rioters-clash-with-police-as-some-schools-flout-virus-lockdown/ (''Times of Israel'')]
****[[Israel]] reports several cases of a [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2|faster-spreading variant]] of [[SARS-CoV-2]], which was recently discovered in the [[United States]]. [https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/coronavirus-israel-live-four-cops-wounded-as-police-clash-with-ultra-orthodox-1.9475784 (''Haaretz'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in India]]
*****The [[Ministry of Health and Family Welfare|Union Health Ministry]] announces that [[India]] has become the fastest nation to reach 1 million doses of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://health.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/industry/one-million-covid-vaccine-doses-administered-in-india-in-just-6-days-health-ministry/80432707 (''The Economic Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 4,427 recoveries in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of recoveries to 141,446. [https://www.theedgemarkets.com/article/new-covid19-cases-drop-3346-recoveries-jump-4427 (The Edge Markets MY)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]], [[Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
*****Around 38 [[United States Capitol Police]] officers have tested positive for [[COVID-19]] since the [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|storming]] of the [[United States Capitol]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/01/24/politics/capitol-police-riot-coronavirus/index.html (CNN)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois]]
*****The [[Chicago]] [[Chicago Teachers Union|Teachers Union]] votes to defy an order by the [[Chicago Public Schools|public schools]] to return to in-person instructions over COVID-19 concerns. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/chicago-teachers-vote-to-teach-remotely-defying-district-order-2021-01-24/ (CBS News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
****[[President of Mexico|Mexican President]] [[Andrés Manuel López Obrador]] announces that he has tested positive for COVID-19 and is receiving medical treatment. [https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSKBN29U02F?il=0 (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Netherlands]], [[Social impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Riot]]ing youths torched a [[COVID-19]] [[COVID-19 testing|testing center]] and threw fireworks at police in the fishing village of [[Urk]] overnight into Sunday. [https://www.dw.com/en/rioting-dutch-youths-torch-covid-testing-center/a-56329339 (DW)]
****[[Riot]]ers set fires in the center of [[Eindhoven]] and pelted police with rocks at a banned [[demonstration (political)|demonstration]] against [[coronavirus lockdown]] measures. [[Law enforcement in the Netherlands|Police]] also faced off with curfew-defying crowds in [[The Hague]], [[Amsterdam]], [[Enschede]], [[Venlo]], [[Stein, Limburg|Stein]], [[Roermond]], [[Oosterhout]], [[Breda]] and elsewhere across the [[Netherlands]]. More than 100 people have been arrested. It was the worst violence to hit the Netherlands since the pandemic began and the second straight Sunday that police clashed with protesters in Amsterdam. The country has been under a lockdown since December. [https://apnews.com/article/netherlands-health-coronavirus-pandemic-riots-amsterdam-550ce0c260d45131181727fbf41e8340 (AP)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-55788924 (BBC News)] [https://www.tasnimnews.com/en/news/2021/01/25/2439357/mass-arrests-as-dutch-riot-police-struggle-to-contain-anti-lockdown-rage-video (Tasnim)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[France]] imposes new border restrictions that require travellers from other [[European Union]] countries arriving by air or sea to present negative [[Polymerase chain reaction|PCR]] [[COVID-19 testing|test results]] obtained in the previous 72 hours. [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20210124-france-imposes-new-border-controls-in-effort-to-curb-spread-of-covid-19 (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] reports a record 275 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 10,469. [https://covid19.min-saude.pt/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/328_DGS_boletim_20210124.pdf (DGS)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Serbia]]
****[[Serbia]] reports their first case of the [[Lineage B.1.1.7|B.1.1.7 variant]] in a person who travelled from [[London]] and later began experiencing mild symptoms. [https://rs.n1info.com/english/news/highly-transmissible-uk-coronavirus-variant-arrives-in-serbia/ (N1)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Egypt]]
***[[Egypt]] launches a [[vaccination]] campaign against [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] with the first doses of [[Sinopharm]]'s [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] given to [[healthcare workers]] in [[Ismailia]]. [https://apnews.com/article/immunizations-health-coronavirus-pandemic-suez-canal-egypt-f65c09c81cc21d847bd441d71a1b2f87 (AP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
***[[New Zealand]] health officials report the first community case of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] in more than two months in a person who travelled from [[Europe]]. [https://www.smh.com.au/world/oceania/new-zealand-reports-first-community-case-in-months-20210124-p56wgm.html (''Sydney Morning Herald'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Russia–United States relations]], [[2021 Russian protests]]
**The [[Government of Russia|Russian government]] accuses the [[United States]] of "interfering in Russian domestic affairs" after some U.S. officials criticized the police crackdown on protests backing jailed opposition leader [[Alexei Navalny]]. [https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-accuses-united-states-interference-navalny-protests/31066416.html (RFERL)]
*[[Cross-Strait relations]]
**For the second consecutive day, [[Taiwan]] reports an incursion of its [[air defense identification zone]] by [[China]]'s [[People's Liberation Army Air Force]]. The incursion involved 12 fighter jets, two anti-submarine aircraft and a reconnaissance plane. Taiwan deployed air defence missile systems in response, according to a statement from the [[Ministry of National Defense (Republic of China)|Ministry of National Defense]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-55788359 (BBC News)]
*[[Israel–United Arab Emirates relations]], [[Israel–United Arab Emirates normalization agreement]]
**[[Israel]] opens an embassy in [[Abu Dhabi]], four months after the signing of the agreement, while the [[United Arab Emirates]] approves the establishment of an embassy in [[Tel Aviv]]. [https://www.dawn.com/news/1603474 (AFP via ''Dawn'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2019–2022 Sudanese protests]]
**Protesters gather in the [[List of cities in Sudan|Sudanese cities]] of [[Khartoum]] and [[Omdurman]] over rising inflation, food shortages, and power cuts in [[Sudan|the country]]. [https://english.aawsat.com/home/article/2763591/protests-sudan-over-worsening-economic-situation (''Asharq Al-Awsat'')]
**[[Law enforcement in Sudan|Sudanese police]] fire tear gas at demonstrators in [[Khartoum]], [[Sudan]], over the country's [[Economy of Sudan|economic]] woes. [https://modernghana.com (Modern Ghana)]
*[[Central African Republic Civil War]]
**The [[Politics of the Central African Republic|Central African government]] renders custody of an alleged [[Séléka]] commander to the [[International Criminal Court]], where he is expected to face charges of [[war crime]]s and [[crimes against humanity]]. [https://www.macaubusiness.com/c-africa-war-crimes-suspect-handed-to-icc-court/ (AFP via ''Macau Business'')]
*[[List of mass shootings in the United States in 2021]]
**A [[mass shooting]] in [[Indianapolis]], [[Indiana]], leaves six dead and one injured. [https://fox59.com/news/multiple-dead-following-shooting-on-indys-near-northeast-side-1-juvenile-critical/ (WXIN-TV)]
*American manufacturer [[Tesla, Inc.|Tesla]] files a lawsuit against one of its former [[software engineer]]s for allegedly copying confidential [[Scripting language|computer scripts]] onto a personal [[file hosting service]]. The former employee denies the company's [[allegation]], claiming he transferred the files by mistake. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/business/01/24/21/tesla-sues-former-employee-for-allegedly-stealing-26000-confidential-files (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Politics of Estonia]]
**The two major political parties [[Estonian Reform Party|Reform Party]] and [[Estonian Centre Party|Centre Party]] agree to form a government, whose [[Prime Minister of Estonia|Prime Minister]] will be [[Kaja Kallas]], who will become the first female to take the office. She is succeeding [[Jüri Ratas]], who resigned following a corruption scandal that involves his party. [https://www.politico.eu/article/estonia-new-government-prime-minister-kaja-kallas/ (''Politico'')]
*[[2021 Portuguese presidential election]]
**[[President of Portugal|Portuguese President]] [[Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa]] is reelected with 60.7% of the vote in Sunday's election. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/exit-poll-incumbent-wins-portugals-presidential-election-75459203 (ABC News)] [https://www.dw.com/en/portugal-votes-in-presidential-election-amid-coronavirus-surge/a-56327656 (DW)]
*[[Proposed second Scottish independence referendum]]
**[[First Minister of Scotland|Scottish First Minister]] [[Nicola Sturgeon]] says she intends to hold a "legal [[referendum]]" on independence since [[Brexit]] removed [[Scotland]] from the [[European Union]] against its will. Another referendum would require the approval of the [[United Kingdom]]'s government, which [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] opposes. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/scotlands-leader-vows-push-independence-vote-75456906 (ABC News)] [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-01-24/sturgeon-seeks-legal-independence-vote-as-party-sets-out-plan (Bloomberg)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[SpaceX]] successfully launches a record 143 satellites into orbit on a single rocket in its ''Transporter-1'' mission. The payload consisted of 120 [[CubeSats]], 12 microsatellites, 10 [[Starlink]] satellites, and 1 transfer stage. It is also the maiden flight of the [[SHERPA (space tug)|SHERPA-FX]] [[satellite dispenser]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/science-environment-55775977 (BBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2020 NFL season]], [[2020–21 NFL playoffs]], [[Super Bowl LV]]
**The [[2020 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] beat the [[2020 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]], 31-26, winning the [[2020 NFC Championship Game|2020]] [[NFC Championship Game|NFC Championship]] and advancing to the [[Super Bowl LV|Super Bowl]]. With the [[Super Bowl]] being held at the [[Raymond James Stadium]] in [[Tampa, Florida|Tampa]], this will be the first time an [[NFL]] team will play the championship game on their home field. They will play the [[2020 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]], who beat the [[2020 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]] 38-24 in the [[AFC Championship Game|2020 AFC Championship]]. [https://www.cbc.ca/sports/football/nfl/nfl-championship-bucs-packers-bills-kansas-city-recap-nfl-1.5886054 (CBC)] [https://apnews.com/article/nfl-sports-tampa-bay-buccaneers-kansas-city-super-bowl-d6f4334e89b9c54f70bf16d0758a6492 (AP)]
